title: UFC: A Unified Accelerator for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Existing FHE accelerators are designed for specific schemes, leading to inefficiency and lack of capability when supporting hybrid-FHE applications that require multiple FHE schemes for different encrypted computations.
motivation: Hybrid-scheme FHE is essential for real-world applications requiring optimal performance and accuracy in post-quantum privacy-preserving computing.
method: The UFC architecture performs comprehensive analysis of FHE processing flows to abstract primitives covering all operations in hybrid FHE applications. It implements hardware function units for these primitives rather than deeply pipelined units, enabling high utilization across schemes. Algorithm-hardware co-optimizations minimize hardware costs for data shuffling patterns, and compiler-level optimizations achieve high hardware utilization across various algorithmic parameter settings.
key_novelty: A unified accelerator architecture that supports multiple FHE schemes through abstracted primitives and high-utilization function units, diverging from previous scheme-specific deeply pipelined designs.
contributions: Comprehensive analysis of FHE processing flows and abstraction of primitives for hybrid-FHE operations
Unified architecture design with hardware function units enabling high utilization across different FHE schemes
Algorithm-hardware co-optimizations for efficient data shuffling in FHE
Compiler-level optimizations for high hardware utilization across varying algorithmic parameters
primary_theme: Unified hardware accelerator for hybrid-scheme FHE
